title: Denial-precedence order differs across impls for multiply-invalid tunnel-auth inputs (diagnostic enum only)
description: Found by kimi-k3 edge-case review of b7z9.93 (pass 3). Wire code is 4.03 in every case across C/Python/Rust, but the denial enum differs for multiply-invalid inputs: (a) accept path - C verifies signature BEFORE egress binding (tunnel_auth.c:358-361), Rust checks egress before signature (tunnel_auth.rs:329-333), so wrong-egress+bad-signature yields 'signature' (C) vs 'wrong-egress' (Rust); (b) decap path - Rust checks source/destination scope BEFORE route validation (tunnel_auth.rs:403-411), C checks route first and scope only after a grant matches (tunnel_auth.c:459-461, 474-477), Python like C (tunnel_auth.py:548-556), so link-local-source+no-grant yields 'source-scope' (Rust) vs 'no-authorization' (C/Python). No security impact (uniform 4.03, fail-closed everywhere; log-only divergence). Resolution: either pin the precedence order in the corpus (add a decap/accept case combining two invalid aspects and align all three) or document precedence as implementation-defined in spec 8.11. Low urgency; file under the tunnel-auth conformance umbrella.
